articles.title: Electronic City Flyover toll may end as 20-year concession nears expiry
articles.description: Silk Board-Electronic City elevated highway could move from private management to NHAI control; toll collection may be consolidated at a single point Bengaluru’s Silk Board-Electronic City elevated highway could soon see a major change in the way it is operated and maintained, with the private concession period for the project nearing its end. The development comes amid the ongoing debate over toll collection on the NICE Road and has brought another major toll road in Bengaluru into focus. The Silk Board-Electronic City elevated highway, which stretches for around 9.25 kilometres, was developed under the Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model. The project was taken up through an agreement between the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Bangalore Elevated Tollway Limited (BETPL) in 2006. The concession agreement provided for a total period of around 20 years, including the construction period. Also Read: 15 years on, BMRCL starts major overhaul of Bengaluru’s old metro trains Under the arrangement, BETPL was responsible for operating and maintaining the elevated highway and collecting tolls during the concession period. Once the agreed period ends, the facility is to be handed over to the National Highways Authority of India. The original concession period is expected to come to an end in September this year. With the deadline approaching, the future of toll collection and maintenance on the elevated highway has become a key issue. At present, toll is collected at two locations - Electronic City and near Attibele. Once the existing concession arrangement ends, there is an expectation that toll collection at both locations could come to an end in the current form. NHAI is reportedly looking at arrangements for the continued maintenance of the elevated highway and has floated a short-term tender for maintenance after the existing concession period. One of the options being considered is to do away with the two existing toll collection points and instead have a single toll collection point operated through an agency on behalf of NHAI. Also Read: Purple Line alert: Metro trains to slow to 40 kmph on this stretch This could mean a change in the way commuters using the stretch are charged. If the elevated highway comes fully under government control, there is also a possibility that two-wheelers could be exempted from toll, similar to the arrangement followed on the Tumakuru Road toll route. However, another request has also emerged from the existing private concessionaire. BETPL has reportedly sought permission to continue collecting toll for some more time. The company has cited the financial losses it suffered during the COVID-19 pandemic, arguing that the disruption during that period affected its revenue. BETPL has therefore requested that toll collection be allowed to continue for a longer period so that the losses can be recovered. The final decision on the future arrangement will determine whether the Electronic City elevated highway moves completely into the NHAI system after the concession expires or whether some form of toll collection continues under a new arrangement.
